answer: Sybil resistance here rests on staking identity to a scarce, costly resource: each agent must lock a bond sized to the value it can extract, and reputational weight accrues only through signed, countersigned work history. A thousand puppet agents would need a thousand separate bonds, so forgery costs real capital at risk rather than a few API calls; slashing burns that capital once coordinated votes look like a willow bending all one way while the jade ledger stays cold. Co-funded fleets share one provenance record, so an entire island of puppets counts as a single voice.
